notes:
Scope enforcement now explicitly applies the host authorization boundary to knowledge layers and recall, with a read-only session-to-project backfill projection; summary writes invalidate the derived overview cache.

## What changed since 0.4.51

- Knowledge-layer reads and recall results are intersected with the host-determined authorization boundary (same rules as the existing hard layers; never widened). Model-supplied project/URI/bank names cannot change permissions.

- A read-only session-to-project backfill projection attributes legacy records without rewriting chat originals; unknown sources stay legacy.

- Summary writes invalidate the derived project-overview cache so a changed source is immediately stale and rebuilt on next read.

- Carries all 0.4.50/0.4.51 features: reply-enhancement horse-head entry (font color off / bottom-up theme ripple generating / solid theme ready, same with evolution on or off), idle-hiding chat scrollbar, at-most-two silent language corrections across main chat, group orchestration, subagents and visible summaries, background memory (progressive recall, recall traces, virtual directory, derived overview, confirmed same-source correction tombstones), stable immutable project IDs, and the Pondsi Attribution License.

## Honest boundaries

- Language detection is heuristic; short or uncertain text is left alone. Enabling the guard adds local checks and up to two extra model calls per task; it does not guarantee compliance and latency differs from the off state.

- Derived memory is not the original record; corrections require evidence and never rewrite chat originals. Model output and generated files still need review. Permissions remain per session; no self-improvement can disable the safety boundaries.

## Install

Download WArmy-Setup-0.4.52.exe from this release and run it. Existing WArmyData carries over. The installer is unsigned; Windows SmartScreen may ask for confirmation. The installer SHA-256 is listed in the Checksum section below. First run stops at the language page and waits for you.
